title: Vertical-Positioning Microlearning
summary: A sanitized short-form sales-learning case study that split a broad industry topic into two focused modules built around operating context, use cases, scenario practice, and follow-up resources.

content.business_need: Help sellers build usable industry context quickly while avoiding a broad vertical course that would be too long for the moment of need.
content.audience: Internal sellers and channel partners who need concise industry context before discovery and positioning conversations.
learning_objectives: Recognize the operating context and common priorities within each industry setting.
Connect customer needs to relevant solution use cases at a sales-ready level.
Practice making a customer-facing decision in a short scenario.
Locate supporting resources for deeper follow-up instead of overloading the lesson.
content.role: Instructional designer and developer responsible for content scoping, learning architecture, build, scenario design, multimedia integration, and review coordination.
content.design_approach: Split the original scope into separate industry modules so each experience could stay focused and short. Reuse a consistent pattern of context, use cases, practice, and resources, and use multimedia only where it supported the learning rather than turning the lesson into a video-first experience.
content.development_process: Built two Rise modules designed to stay under seven minutes, added scenario practice and a short AI-presenter video as one supporting element, and coordinated internal QA plus specialist review for each industry area. The structure was refined when the original combined scope proved too broad.
outcomes: Turned one broad vertical topic into two focused modules with clearer boundaries and shorter learner paths.
Created a repeatable short-form pattern that connects context, use cases, practice, and follow-up resources.
Used specialist review and scoped multimedia to keep the content useful without adding unnecessary depth.

source_material_notes: Generalized from documented industry-focused sales enablement work. Industry-specific proprietary messaging, internal screenshots, customer details, reviewer comments, dates, links, and source material are intentionally omitted.
